findings.finding: The plan assumes the CI Jira account can create and delete REB versions over REST, but it never checks that the account has the needed permission. If the bot account lacks Administer Projects on REB, every new test fails at setup. Worse, a version could be created and then fail to delete, which defeats the cleanup guarantee.

findings.finding: The plan extends the workflow's always-run cleanup step to delete run-prefixed REB versions 'with curl' but doesn't say how curl gets JIRA_API_TOKEN or that its output must stay out of the logs. Today that step uses only acli with its stored login, so curl adds a new path where the token is sent explicitly. GitHub hides only the literal secret value. If the step uses set -x, curl -v or --trace, the log shows the base64 Basic auth header, which GitHub does not hide and anyone who can read the job log can decode. The plan also doesn't make curl require HTTPS for the JIRA_URL repo variable.
findings.location: Implementation notes → Versions ('The workflow's existing cleanup step does the same with curl'); .github/workflows/external-integration.yml 'Sweep any leaked throwaway Cloud issues' step
scenarios: A maintainer adds set -x or curl -v to debug a failing sweep, and the base64 Basic auth header lands in a run log that every repo reader can see.
JIRA_URL is set to an http:// value by mistake and curl sends the credential in plaintext.
findings.suggested_fix: In the cleanup step, call curl with `-fsS --proto '=https' -u "$JIRA_USER:$JIRA_API_TOKEN"`, using the existing secrets.JIRA_API_TOKEN env mapping. Don't use set -x, -v or --trace in that step. Extend tests/unit/test_external_integration_cloud_mutation_workflow.py to assert that those options are present and that no verbose or trace options appear.
